original_test_intent: Execute one approved Redfish Manager ForceRestart against the exact BMC and prove the Manager resets successfully, management connectivity is interrupted exactly once and the same BMC recovers healthy.
original_method: Discover Manager.Reset and its ActionInfo/allowable values, establish BMC/network baseline and recovery access, obtain approval, send one secure ForceRestart POST, measure a timestamped outage sequence using independent signals and validate post-reset Redfish identity/health without retry.
manual_activity: The owner approves the disruptive BMC reset/window and one-disconnect measurement contract; an operator monitors independent recovery and authorizes any escalation.
required_inputs: Exact BMC/Manager identity, firmware and discovered Reset action/ActionInfo
ForceRestart allowable-value semantics and expected action response
Definition/sampling resolution for exactly one network disconnect versus timeouts/link flaps
Pre/post BMC session/network/Redfish health baseline and recovery deadline
Independent console/recovery/escalation procedure, TLS trust and protected credential
safety_requirements: Verify exact BMC and action target before explicit just-in-time approval
Use certificate validation/protected secrets; never -k, root password literal or guessed URI
Issue exactly one ForceRestart and never retry on response loss or timeout
Monitor through an independent path and stop/escalate on absent/repeated interruption or recovery failure
Preserve pre/post BMC/network/Redfish logs and avoid concurrent firmware or management operations
agent_execution_scope: Discover/validate Manager/action/schema/ForceRestart support and collect baseline
After explicit approval, POST one exact ForceRestart and capture response/audit
Monitor network and Redfish reachability with approved sampling until bounded recovery
Count interruptions under the owner rule and verify same-BMC identity/health after recovery
Package evidence without retry or independent DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve reset target/window, interruption measurement and recovery deadline
Supervise independent recovery and decide any outage escalation
Review one-shot reset, outage count and post-health evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: ResetActionInfo is a valid pre-check but cannot satisfy a testcase requiring actual reset, recovery and exactly one interruption. The source POST also needs discovery and secure transport instead of hardcoded URI/credentials/-k.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Securely discover the Manager.Reset target and ForceRestart support, obtain approval, issue one POST and correlate the response with bounded multi-signal outage/recovery telemetry and post-reset identity/health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Manager ForceRestart, successful reset, exactly one network disconnect and 5/5-minute estimates remain; actual approved recovery deadline may supersede the estimate without erasing it.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a one-shot state machine: healthy baseline, accepted action, connectivity loss onset, one contiguous outage interval, service/certificate/firmware identity recovery and healthy final snapshot, all on a synchronized clock.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds action discovery, secure credentials/TLS, an explicit interruption-count algorithm and independent bounded recovery instead of manual behavior observation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Action metadata or a successful POST response cannot prove the BMC reset. Conversely, one missed ping is not necessarily a network disconnect; a defined contiguous outage and recovered same-BMC identity are required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Reset intentionally removes management access and can interrupt active operations. Sampling frequency affects interruption counting, and retrying during recovery can cause a second outage.

project_override_considerations: If management networking has redundant paths or expected multiple protocol-level drops within one physical reset, the approved counting rule must define one logical interruption without weakening the source criterion.
expected_evidence: Exact source row/variant/hash and BMC/Manager/firmware/certificate/network identity
Action target/ActionInfo/ForceRestart support and owner approval
Pre-reset Redfish/network/session baseline and redacted one-shot POST response/audit
Synchronized reachability/link/ARP-route timeline with exactly-one-interruption calculation
Same-BMC post-reset service/identity/health, outage duration, no-retry audit, recovery and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria coherently require a Manager ForceRestart, successful recovery and one network disconnection. DeepSeek's read-only shortcut is incomplete but does not alter the authoritative source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Approval, telemetry and recovery package gate execution, yet the static review is complete and can proceed without treating missing project inputs as hardware failure.

review_improvement: Restores the mutation omitted by DeepSeek and makes exactly-one interruption and same-BMC recovery measurable, bounded and non-retriable.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BMC reset can make the action response disappear before completion, so loss of the HTTP session is neither failure nor proof of success. The required causal chain is an accepted one-shot action, one contiguous management outage under a defined sampler, then recovery of the same BMC identity and healthy Redfish service. TCP, link and ARP/route observations distinguish a BMC service outage from client/network noise. A second reset would create another interruption and invalidate both safety and the criterion.
